review_text: I'll start by saying my friend and I were hesitant to even join a tour (given the negative things that we had read about some of the different tour companies online) but we were recommended to do it by lots of travellers that we had met. World White Travel was one of the companies recommended by our hostel in San Pedro so we decided to book with them. We didn't know what to expect but we are so glad we booked with them. The first day started with us taking a shuttle from San Pedro de Atacama to the border to cross into Bolivia, have breakfast and meet our drivers. We got divided into 2 groups with our group's driver being Renaldo. He ended up also being our (fantastic by the way) cook, guide, photographer and DJ. That day and the next day we toured the desert seeing the different lagunas, volcanoes, rock formations and flamingos! The last (and everybody's favorite) day we drove out onto the Uyuni salt flat before sunrise. This was one of the highlights of my South American trip so far. Our whole group had a blast. Renaldo made sure to take us to places where there were very few other tour groups around so we could enjoy the areas more. He also drove out of the way on the last day to find water on the salt flats so that we could take better pictures. All in all it was a fantastic tour and I would definitely do it with this is company again. If you can; try to request Renaldo as your guide. He definitely went the extra mile to make sure that everyone had an amazing time.

review_text: I contacted Antilco nearly eight months prior to the date of the four day Rio Blanc horse trek. I booked approximately six months beforehand. Before and after booking - we were in good periodic communication. After arriving on the ranch we sat for a quick breakfast and a briefing on the day's ride. At breakfast - I found Mathias to be warm and genial. The crew - Carmen and Anna made us feel welcomed. There were 7 of us plus two horsewomen to accompany the ride. After perhaps over three hour ride - we returned to the ranch for a hearty lunch. After finishing up lunch we (my riding buddy) and I were summoned into the office. The first thing out of Mathias' mouth was - "We have a problem". Turns out Mathias apparently became jittery over the fact of our deafness. Mathias wanted us to pay an additional $580 dollars (CH$275,000) to get an additional rider to accompany us plus to cover the apparent additional expense of another vehicle and other equipment. We didn't see this train coming and sat there momentarily trying to absorb the enormity of the prejudice and discrimimnation that just struck us. Mathias felt our deafness was a medical condition and a physical limitation upon the ride. [Deafness is neither a medical condition nor a physical limitation to riding a horse]. His attempt to "accommodate" felt like an attempt to extract additional funds against a supposedly vulnerable population as well as supposedly trapped customers having invested and traveled thus far from the States and likely to cough up the additional funds to preserve the "investment". Mathias may suffer from a greater mental limitation of prejudice towards the physically disabled. Be forewarned - if you're obese; if you got a prosthesis leg; or if you're wearing a pacemaker - any apparent medical or handicap - you're more likely to be asked to pay more to cover his imagined expenses. There was no indication of any real sustained difficulty with communication with the crew on the shakedown ride. I now realize the initial ride isn't only to help with matching the horse to the rider but may be a ploy used to screen customers in an attempt to find justifications for additional monies under the guise of safety and responsibility. I explained to Mathias that I'm fully informed of the various riding conditions - having read numerous horse trekking blogs as well as TripAdvisor reviews of numerous horse trekking outfits. I complied with his policy to obtain travel insurance and we also signed his waiver form prior to the ride. Mathias labeled both of us as inept riders. I'd ridden horses over the course of my life. review_text: Find the bus counters and buy two tickets from the "Tur Bus" counter to "Estacion Pajaritos." Walk to the end of the hallway that the bus counters are in, walk outside and to the right, then walk down for a while until you find "Salida 5" where green "Tur Bus" busses will be waiting. (Along the way at least three staff offered us help getting to the correct bus.) Ask if they go to Pajaritos, and if they do, give the driver your tickets and get on the bus then get off at the first stop. Find the Tur Bus counter at the station and buy a ticket for the next bus to Valparaiso. (There are timing logistics in buying a ticket straight to Valparaiso and if the bus is late, you’ll have to buy another ticket) Get on that bus and it will take you to the station in Valparaiso. Many taxis outside the station are available.

review_text: Choosing a salt flats tour company (from San Pedro to Uyuni) was a very difficult decision for my girlfriend and I because of all of the horror stories out there. However, after doing some research we decided to go with World White Travel and could not be happier. We have nothing but good things to say! Firstly, we were not "pawned off" on another tour company at the Bolivia border like other companies do. There were 12 people and we travelled in two separate WWT 4x4 vehicles. We were allowed to choose our groups. Our group turned out to be a lot of fun! Secondly, the food was delicious for the most part - fresh soups, vegetables, chicken, tuna. There was also lots of tea and coffee (including coca tea). Thirdly, the price was very competitive with the other companies (if not cheaper). Fourthly, WWT has offices in both San Pedro and Uyuni (unlike other companies) so if you have any complaints you can speak with the representative at your arrival point. Lastly and most importantly, our guide, Nefi, was absolutely amazing. Throughout the tour he really went out of his way for us and worked extremely hard. For example, he made sure that we beat the other groups to the hot showers on our second night of the tour. He was very funny and also provided us with lots of information for the sights. He also adapted the schedule to our group's preferences. He took great photos for us at the salt flats. Finally, he spoke English!! (which is very rare with the other guides). I highly recommend WWT. Also, you should request Nefi as your guide (it doesn't hurt to ask). You will not regret it.

review_text: We loved this trip, one of the most amazing places we've been. Miguel was our driver/guide, he's great, funny, kind, a safe driver, explained everything we saw and answered all our questions. He also played great music. We always had fresh fruit and vegetables. Accommodations were simple and comfy. Tip: departing from San Pedro you will get picked up in a mini bus with all the other travellers, you will spend hours with them before entering Bolivia where you meet the drivers and transfer to the landcruisers. Before you get to the Bolivian border is your time to meet others and make your group of 6 for the trip, so start talking to them and find like minded people. Once at the border they will ask who wants to go together in each landcruiser. We were lucky to make a great group, but others were not as lucky.

review_text: Assim que comprei nossas passagens para o Deserto do Atacama entrei em contato por WhatsApp com a Atacama Desert Stargazing. A resposta foi muito rápida com orientações preciosas: pelas datas da viagem o Jorge disse que teria apenas 1 dia que seria perfeito. E foi... um tour PERFEITO! Pontos positivos👍🏻: - agilidade nas respostas e orientações via WhatsApp: Eu estava apreensiva com o passeio, mas depois que iniciei as conversas com o Jorge, este me passou bastante confiança, esclareceu todas as minhas dúvidas, sempre muito educado e paciente - pontualidade O carro foi super pontual ao nos buscar no hotel, momento em que finalmente conhecemos o Jorge (ele mesmo estava dirigindo). - paciência Fomos em 4 pessoas, sendo meus pais (ambos de 71 anos) e 1 criança (12 anos), e todos nós com um conhecimento pequeno do céu, conhecimento adquirido em leituras de revista, sites, aplicativos de celular. Quando o Jorge iniciou sua aula foram surgindo muitas dúvidas e ele esclareceu e explicou todas... pacientemente, pois nós falamos português e ele espanhol. Então, ele falava lentamente, gesticulava, traduzia... até que a gente entendesse!!!! - conhecimento A aula que o Jorge dá foi, para nós, incrível. O entusiasmo com que ele fala nos contagia, nos prende a atenção de uma forma que quase ignoramos o frio. - telescópios O local possui muitos telescópios... eu não lembro, mas vi muitos corpos celestes, muitos mesmos. Mas se quiserem saber quantos telescópios têm, perguntem para o Jorge... certeza que ele responderá!!! - lanche Depois de um tempo congelando no frio da noite no deserto nos deparamos com duas mesas, uma de snacks e bebidas quentes e outra só de bebidas. Um lanchinho bem bom e bebidas quentinhas... nos aqueceu bastante para continuar nosso tour. - local: Cadeiras com cobertores quentinhos para ouvirmos a aula, banheiros químicos, área plana, fácil de andar entre os telescópios. - fotos As fotos ficaram ótimas e adivinhem quem as tirou??? Sim, o Jorge!!!!! Ponto negativo: - o frio!!! Apesar de estarmos com roupas que em outra viagem enfrentamos -20°C passamos frio aqui, porque nesse tour ficamos sentados e parados (na outra viagem estávamos no frio, mas em constante movimento, nos esquentando mais). Então, agasalhem-se! Bom, no nosso tour vimos a via láctea, constelações (que o Jorge fez a gente enxergar), planetas (Venus e Saturno) e a lua. O Jorge havia nos avisado que a lua nasceria depois das 23h, então, até esse horário vimos tudo, tiramos as fotos... mas ficamos mais depois que a lua nasceu, pois o Jorge nos mostrou a beleza desse nosso satélite natural e ainda tirou fotos dela com nossos celulares. Esse tour valeu muito a pena... faria de novo, com certeza. English version 😉 As soon as I bought my tickets to go to the Atacama Desert, I contacted Atacama Desert Stargazing via WhatsApp. The answer was very quick with precious instructions: by the dates of the trip, Jorge said that only have 1 specific day would be perfect. So it was... a PERFECT tour! What was positive about the tour 👍🏻: - agility in responses and guidance via WhatsApp: I was apprehensive about the tour, but after I started talking to Jorge, he gave me a lot of confidence, clarified all my doubts, always very polite and extremely patient - punctuality The car was super punctual when picking us up from the hotel, at which point we finally met Jorge (he was driving himself 😊). - patience We were 4 people, my parents (both 71 years old) and 1 child (12 years old), and all of us with a little knowledge of the sky. This knowledge was acquired from reading magazines, websites, cell phone applications. When Jorge started his class, many doubts arose and he clarified and explained them all... very patiently, because we speak Portuguese and he speaks Spanish. So, he had to spoke slowly, gestured and sometimes translate what he was saying... until we understood!!!! - knowledge The class that Jorge gives was, for us, incredible. The enthusiasm with which he speaks was contagious, holding our attention in such a way that we almost ignore the cold. - telescopes The place has many telescopes... I don't remember, but I saw many astronomical objects, many of them. But if you want to know how many telescopes they have, ask Jorge... I'm sure he'll answer!!! - snack After freezing for a while in the cold of the night in the desert, we found two tables, one for snacks and hot drinks and the other just for drinks. A very good snack and warm drinks... warmed us up enough to continue our tour. - local: Chairs with warm blankets to listen to the class, chemical toilets, flat area, easy to walk between the telescopes. - Photos The pictures turned out great and guess who took them??? Yes, it was George!!!!! What was not good in the tour: - the cold!!! Although we were wearing clothes that on another trip we faced -20°C, we were cold here. On this tour we were sitting and still (on the other trip we were in the cold, but in constant movement, warming up more). So, please wear all your warm clothes! On our tour we saw the milky way, constellations (which Jorge made us see), planets (Venus and Saturn) and the moon. Jorge had warned us that the moon would rise after 11 pm, so until that time we saw everything, he took pictures of us... but we stayed longer after the moon rose, because Jorge showed us the beauty of our natural satellite and even took pictures of her with our cell phones. This tour was really worth it... I would definitely do it again. Thank you very much for everything!!

review_text: This 3 hour tour guided by Sebastian was very informative, interesting and fun! We reviewed the important historical aspects of Valparaiso without digging too far. None of the historical facts were boring, they all introduced special aspects of the city and why it is such a special place. Although 3 hours sounds like a long time, it flew by. Valparaiso is a city filled with stories and history. We had an opportunity to take the hill elevator, which was really neat. The elevators are unique to Valparaiso and give a breath taking view of the sea and the hill side fill with houses. We also learned about the history of the hills, there are over 40 hills and they each have quirky stories. Sebastian provided useful information about how these hills developed their names and individual culture. Sebastian is a well of information and was very friendly to each tourist. He made sure to introduce himself to each person on the tour. We stopped by a local shop for pisco sours and empanadas during the tour which was a nice break. He has an excellent grasp on the English language which was helpful since the tour was attended by english speakers from all over the world. My only qualm is that I had additional questions for Sebastian and he provided me with an incorrect phone number! Other then that, I highly recommend this tour! and visiting Valparaiso!

review_text: Le Sebastiana was the former home of the Nobel prize winner Pablo Neruda, this mainly for his poetry. It is now a museum following being restored in 1991 after having been looted during the military coup of 1973. It is located on Florida Hill with great views over to the port and out to sea. We assume it was converted to a museum in honour of Neruda but also for its wackiness for it contains some odd pieces such as a wooden merry go round horse and a music box as well as a collection of pictures and old maritime maps. There are also a number of items with very much a naval theme as well as a few copies of his poetry. To us, it reminded us of Dali’s house in Portlligat, Spain as that is now a museum and like La Sebastiana houses a lot of memorabilia along with many items reflecting the artists wackiness. Both are worth visiting.

review_text: I booked a tour of one week on the Carretera Austral for me and my mom and payed with o month's advance. After I had payed the attendants from the agency simply stopped returning my e-mails, even when I was already in the tour and had doubts, I had to ask the guide to talk to the agency for me, because they still wouldn't answer any e-mail. If we left earlier from the hotels, we would definitely arrive earlier on the attractions and could spend more time and get to know more of the Carretera, not only from inside the van. The only good hotel that we stayed was "Espacio y Tiempo" at La Junta, all the other ones were really bad. When we arrived at our last destination, Puyuhuapi, me and my mom stayed in a nice cabin with kitchen, but all the others from the group stayed at a horrible hostel, they were all complaining, with reason, because the package is not cheap at all. The guides and the drivers are super kind and dedicated, but I wouldn't recommend the tour or the agency to anyone, it was a bad experience and most of the other people on the tour with us agreed, specially since the quality of the hotels decreased day after day.

review_text: I booked two full days with the team to discover the patagonian wildlife and try to watch the elusive puma. In all our emails, Carla was very reactive despite many reschedulements due to Covid. On the day D, Miguel and Juan Pablo came to pick me up by car at 5:30 and we drove on the road of the End of the World to reach Torres del Paine. This tour is perfect is you want multiple photography opportunities. We took the time to do several stops at nice lookouts for sunrise and sunset. The guides spotted nandous, several species of birds, guanacos and two pumas. The tracking in itself is very informative and interesting. You learn how these big cats live, the best hours and methods to spot them. We used mainly the car to cover large distances and be more efficient in our research. As the land is mainly private owned, we are not supposed to leave the road and the hiking trails. At the end, we saw a puma for a few minuts and at a distance the first day and we managed to spend around 3 hours with another puma the second day. Miguel and Juan Pablo are very friendly, they put all our energy and motivation in providing the most educational and unique experience and it creates then a lifetime adventure. Muchas gracias !

review_text: I booked a tour through Viator because I read excellent reviews here. Actually our trip was wonderful (Cajon del Maipo and San Jose Volcan). The trip was organized and executed by the local agency AndoAndes. I must say that what Viator offered (and what I payed for) is a bit different from what we got: they said max 8 peaple, but indeed the group was 13 people in a kind of minivan...not very confortable, especially because I was sitting in the middle between people, not ideal for enjoying the landscapes. They said that we will have lunch in a mountain refuge but we had a packed lunch. It was great anyway, very fresh sandwiches with fruit and dessert and we ate it during the hiking trip, but just it was not what Viator offered. We had a coffe/drink at the refuge in the afternoon on the way back to Santiago. Finally, most of the the other participants booked directly at AndoAndes (for example through their hotel facility) and they payd much less than me (I payed 110$ while they payed 90$ directly to the guide). Moreover there was a problem with the management of the reservation between Viator and AndoAndes and I was "forgotten" at the hotel. I waited one hour and then I called them: they said that my name was not there, but I had the booking confirmation; so they ent an additional car to bring me to the tour start. This was quite disappointing.

review_text: This is the most interesting architecture of any building in Valparaiso. It is an eclectic hodgepodge of Byzantine, Tudor, Bavarian, and who-knows-what-else influences and is worth slowly strolling around to take in the embellishments that characterize every side and angle. It doesn't hurt that the paseo on three sides affords beautiful views of Valparaiso and usually features local artists and musicians. The palace contains a museum of Chilean art. If it's a rainy day, it is worth stopping in for 40 minutes to view art that is fine but that isn't about to make it into non-Chilean art history classes.

review_text: I had a bad experience with this tour. I took 2 tours with Ecotour, the first one was to Isla Damas which was very good but this one was a total disappointment! It started off pretty good, however it became annoying and ended up with a horrible experience. This tour was with a tour guide named Jorge also, but a bigger sized man with blond/white hair. I have to admit, his explanations were good at the start. He explained things well and was very informative. However, as time passed by, i dont know if he got lazy or what, he explained less and less in English. The tour was in a bus, about 20 people and only my friend and i were the people who does not understand Spanish. We were unhappy because he explained in Spanish for like 15mins and in English only in 5mins. We thought, okay, could be the language thats why it was longer. But we were unhappy because he should have switched in between instead of explaining the whole lot in Spanish, then only in English. While in the bus, a few sights came up and he explained in Spanish, then only he mentioned in English, did you see that just now? It was something something. Of course some of it we didnt manage to see because we didnt understand and we didnt even know where to look! But yes, some places where the bus slowed down, he did managed to explain them very well. I give him credits to that but he should be more professional like the other tour guides that says look there in both languages so people get to see it and then quickly explain in both languages instead of explaining every detail in 1 language then only switching languages. That's not the worst part, he explained something in Spanish for 25mins and he said he will explain it in English after that. But after that he did not. My friend and i were very unhappy, when we got down the bus, we asked him what happened to the English explanation? He said he will explain it later. Ok fine, then when we were at the distillery, he did well in the 1st part, explaining the process, how the machines work, the temperatures, etc. But when we moved on to the tunnel which some holes in the wall, he did not explain one single thing in english. Then moved on to the room with the piscos stored with some history of some ghostly pictures there. It's like we know half and dont know half. We were very unhappy so we complained to the agency and asked them to do something about it, but we did not know it was the end of the trip and the last stop was lunch and a small square of shops. During lunch, i was called out by the tour guide, he confronted me and asked me why did i complain to his agency. I explained i was unhappy that he did not explain much in English but he told me "my boss said you didnt receive any information in English". I could prove the the entire world (its a msg in whatsapp) that i did not say i didnt get ANY information. I explained i was unhappy we got only 5 mins of explanations while he explained 10 to 15mins in Spanish. Although we were a minority, but we still paid, didnt we? So unfair! Then i mentioned, what happened to the 25mins of explanation you said you were going to translate? He said he planned on translating it on our journey down. And he said he guess its a misunderstanding thats why i complained and he asked if i could help him by saying i misunderstood him to help reduce his penalty. But hey! The journey down is normally when everyone is too darn tired to listen, that's when he want to explain. Ridiculous! It should not be like that. Anyway, i wanted to help him because i did not want to cause so much problems to him so i agreed i will help him, but i wanted to do it after the entire trip when i am free at night. So yeah, after lunch, while on the way down, guess what? I stayed awake to wait for him to explain and he didnt explain a single thing! I was so pissed! I did not further complain. And finally, the most horrible thing happened. He did not drop us right at our accomodation, he dropped us 5 minutes walk away and said this is our stop. When the bus stopped, we did not move from our seats because we dont recognize that stop at all, it was not the same place he picked us up. Then he yelled, well are you going down? This is your stop. You can ask ALL the passengers in the bus as evidence! Then on the way down, as always, i said thank you, even though i didnt enjoy it. He did not even say thank you nor did he bid farewell, he immediately turned his back towards us and went up the bus. Totally unprofessional of him to do such a thing! Thank goodness i did not help him immediately during lunch, otherwise it would be even angrier! To Ecotour agency: i am very sure you know which person am i, and i would like you to investigate on this issue. Ask the people on the bus, gain all evidence you can. If you have a camera on the bus, please check on it! Please also check if there is a camera outside the restaurant where he confronted me. All evidence is there. Do something about it, dont let this guy spoil the reputation of your company. He really did make me think that it was the worst tour ever! To the tour guide, i honestly felt you explained well, during the stops, but not all. You should not have done what you did and you should have apologized at one point instead of purely confronting me that what you did was right. you have to be more fair to the minorities not just focus on the majority. The minorities paid too!

review_text: Museo de la Memoria y los Derechos Humanos (The Museum of Memory & Human Rights) is shocking and confronting but excellent. This is the must do museum in Santiago. Take the green subway line to Quinta Nomal. The museum is on the left, across the road as you exit the station. You will have to check your bag and no photos are allowed. Also be advised that identification is required by at least one person in your party. The exhibits are in Spanish but you can hire an inexpensive interactive guide for around $2 (2000 pesos). Allow yourself 2-3 hours - trust me, you'll need it. Be warned, this museum is the Chilian equivalent of a visit to Auschwitz - something that may not be enjoyable but should definately be done to help prevent this ever happening again.

review_text: The Valle del Equi is worth the 2 1/2 hour bus ride from La Serena, however, ensure you travel on a Friday or Saturday as the towns in the Valle are much more lively. Mon to Thur, a lot of shops and restaurants close early or are not even open. I recommend hiring bikes and riding around the Valle; there is a tourist info shop that hires bikes for approx. 40,000Cl and drops you off at the top of the Valle and allows you to ride down. It's a nice bike ride back, takes approx. 2 hours and that includes stops at a winery and two distilleries. If you want to stay local, there are other places that hire bikes for cheaper and multiple hostels to choose from.

We ended up doing the 54km downhill mountain bike stopping into the towns, pisco distilleries, a winery and a brewery and more. They drop you into the valley (so you don’t have to bike the uphill!). Such a fantastic way to see and experience the extremely beautiful area! We ran out of daylight hours to do everything though so if you like to potter about and see all the wee boutique shops in Pisco Elki and Montenegro then you might want to do the shorter bike if you take a tour during shorter daylight hours. Also to note about the distance -the biking is not difficult so don’t worry. You cruise downhill most of the way. Both Adeline and Lincoln make the experience seamless and so memorable. Thanks! Laura and George from New Zealand x

review_text: I was fortunate to have perfect weather, so my memories of TdP are ones of sunny blue skies, snow topped peaks, crystal clear water in the streams (delicious to scoop up with your hands and drink) and green hillsides covered in flowers. I was apprehensive when I started out on the W hike, being a female hiking alone, but it was absolutely fine and I never felt unsafe. Infact, I ended up loving the freedom of hiking where I wanted, when I wanted and at the pace I wanted. I would also like to acknowledge a staff member at the Fantastico Sur office in Puerto Natales. I had been unwell for days before arriving in PN and was disorganised regarding the hiking options at TdP, but needed to figure a plan out and organise it within 1-2 hours. I went into the Fantastico Sur office and was met by the incredibly helpful Daniela (who claimed she didn't speak much English, but was too hard on herself). Daniela gave realistic advice about the hiking, helped me with my accommodation and even helped with onward bus advice because she used to work for one of the bus companies. I so appreciated her friendly nature and help, it was just what I needed and helped to ensure I had a most memorable time in TdP. If you are looking for TdP advice when in PN, I can recommend visiting Daniela at the Fantastico Sur office (on Esmeralda).

review_text: The staff at my hotel (Hotel Altiplanico) highly recommended this tour, and since I have been extremely pleased with their service thus far, I happily took their suggestion. I was very satisfied with the tour and even more so that it was a small group of 5 people in a minivan. Our guide, Martin, was very knowledgeable and friendly. He shared a lot of facts on the drive to Valparaiso and during the walking tour there. Of note: Valparaiso was very foggy and chilly in the morning, so consider bringing a light jacket. There are 2 funicular rides that you need small change to pay the admission, so try and have some 100 peso coins. We stopped at a restaurant in Viña del Mar. I had an amazing paella and glass of the local Sauvignon Blanc. It was a bit pricy at 19,000 pesos, as this is a tourist/resort town. You could pay with credit card. The winery tour and tasting was standard for a winery. You can buy bottles there, but there is no shipping option. Of note: the winery does distribute to the USA market (their main distributer is located in NJ), so you might be able to find it in some places. Would highly recommend the tour! We are very happy you enjoy this tour with us we will congrat Martin for his job

review_text: I've actually waited more than a month before posting my review since I was so mad at this company I wanted to wait and calm down in order to be civil. But as I write this I find my blood is already boiling and I hope to keep it together as this was the most unpleasant experience in all my years of travelling. I find nothing good to say about this tour and this company and wish tripadvisor would offer a zero-star rating as I find one star way too generous. We took the Ruta del Sol trip. I tried to book online but had to go into the office to finish the booking. I did indicate online that we requested an english tour and when I went to the office it was quite obvious that my spanish is rudimentary and understanding spanish is difficult for my - and my spouse has no knowledge of english. So why did the person who attended to me not say that english would not be provided? I didn't ask because the website asked what language I requested so I assumed it would be offered. Big mistake I'll never repeat. So the day of the tour as the guide made his round and asked me if I spoke spanish I said very little and my spouse said no. He said he would speak spanigh slowly. Well that lasted a whole of 30 seconds and then he proceded to speak in spanish at lightening fast speed so we didn't undestand anything he said. He didn't seem to care for he completely ignored us for the rest of the trip. His apathy was so obvious that a chilian family from Santiago took pity on us and explained some things to us in english - wow these are the type of people who should work in the tourism industry. Not the people working at Magical Tours - by the way do not be swayed by the name of the company in english as this is deceptively misleading. And finally, the tour that was sold to us was not delivered. The Ruta del Sol tour clearly shows that it includes a visit to the Geoflifos de Pintados - THE reason why we took this tour. But we didn't go there at all, not even close. When I pointed it out to the guide (who had by then decided to nap at the back of the bus) he blurted out in machine-gun spanish that we had seen one geoflifo at the side of the highway outside Iquique! At this point I was too tired and mad to argue with him and this would have been pointless. So Magical Tours Chile lies about the tours it offers. So this company basically stole our money. Since I'm forced to give a one-star rating to this tour I must find something to justify it, so I'll say that the bus was confortable. review_text: We went on two day trips with Frank. We had checked out the website and said we wanted to do the Maule valley waterfalls walk and the Enladrillado walk. Frank suggested we do the waterfalls walk first, as it is an easier walk. We had a fabulous day. There's a number of quite big waterfalls, and the countryside around is quite bare, so it makes a great contrast. Having had a chance to see our general fitness, Frank had a chat with us about the kinds of things we wanted to see, and suggested that another option - Cerro Paine - would be better for us than the Enladrillado walk. Cerro Paine is a solid climb - 1200 metres up - but the climb is really interesting with differing woodland and above-tree-line scenery, and the view from the top was amazing. You can see Laguna del Alto and for a long way in all directions. We really recommend Frank. He was a great guide, not only talking with us and offering options to get the closest to the experiences we were after, but also carefully keeping check that things were going okay during the walk. He was punctual with pickups from our hostel.

review_text: The history behind this winery is as interesting as the wines themselves. Founded in 1884 by Domingo Fernández Concha, it was here that General Bernardo O’Higgins and his 120 soldiers took refuge after a battle against the forces of the Spanish Crown. The setting is spectacular, and the formal gardens are beautiful. Even though it is a large winery, you feel the intimacy of their love for the quality wines they produce. The taste proves it out. Our tour guide was very knowledgeable, taking us from the vineyards to the bottling area and everything in between. The gift shop is compact but has some unique things as well as the wonderful wines. A nice half day side trip from Santiago. review_text: Just down the road from Caldera is this gorgeous beach with its white sands and turquoise waters. This is the South Pacific so the water is COLD. Too cold for us to dip in in early April but several brave souls did! Amongst the sand are black rocks that give the bay character but rock shoes are by no means necessary. It gets a bit windy but never too cold to lie and sunbathe in the strong light. Parking is free along the esplanade and there are several restaurants. There is a boardwalk from the road into the beach and is suitable for wheelchair users as well. The beach was clean when we visited. No litter anywhere. But there are several stray dogs, though not vicious but rather friendly and playful (if a bit mangy). This is a great place to spend a day and one of the most beautiful beaches in Chile. Definitely recommended.

review_text: We took their Vina del Mar and Valparaiso full day tour. Everything worked well in this well-organised tour. They pick you up at your hotel/B&B at the appointed time in vans which just transfer you to a central point at Parque Arauco where buses and vans await with their respective excursions names visibly marked. This is much better than having buses going from hotel to hotel in traffic for hours picking up passengers. The departure time was exactly as predicted and so was the return when the whole process is reversed. The day we went on this excursion our guide was Jacqueline which related everything in Spanish and English. The guide was informative without being overbearing. Moreover she had a sense of humour and interacted well with the passengers. Since this is a popular tour, a large bus was used. The bus was comfortable and driven well by the motorist. There were sufficient number of stops to have bathroom breaks and leg stretching and there was also a walking section in Valparaiso which was the best part of the tour. I wish it were longer... For lunch we stopped at the Casino where, if they so wished, passengers could have a buffet lunch at a special discounted price: the food was fine and there was a large array of delicious desserts. The price was right as we would not have done any better going to another restaurant. I would recommend this tour and this company if you have a limited time and want a day trip away from Santiago. Moreover, if you book through the internet you get a 10% discount. Thank you very much for sharing your experience! We are very happy that you had a great time with our team and we appreciate your feedback that allows other travelers to know the details of our services. Looking forward to welcoming you again for example on a trip to discover Valparaiso more deeply, all the best. The Turistik team

review_text: This temple is located at the west end of Gregorio Cordovez Street, half a block from the Plaza de Armas of La Serena, in a classic Mannerist style. It really has an incredible story. It was originally built in 1675, but was destroyed in 1686 by the English pirate Edward David when he hid in his cloister after his plan to take over La Serena failed. The temple was rebuilt in limestone and put into service around 1775, and years later, in 1821, the first Chilean regional high school was opened in its premises, and the second in the country after the National Institute in Santiago, which would later be moved and transformed. at the La Serena Men's High School. What draws a lot of attention is its bell tower, built in a style called eclectic.

If y´all are still in Chile, I highly recommend checking out the walking tours from our sister company, Tours4Tips, which are in Valparaíso, San Pedro de Atacama, and Viña del Mar, in addition to Santiago. We booked a Penguin Tour with the first company we say. There are 7 boat operators but all charge the same (7,000 pesos per person). They gave us a life vest and loaded us on a special people carrier that was then pushed through the water to the boat where we embarked. The tour was approx 30 minutes and was simply stunning. review_text: I had a chance to visit Chiloe for two days and had to tour the island alone. Before I left the US, I searched for local tours that started from Castro, where I would be, and I found that most of the Chiloe tours left from Puerto Montt, and a few that left from Castro required a minimum of 2 travelers. But luckily, when I was in Castro and talked to TI office, I found Chiloe Etnico, a local tour company who was willing to take me alone. I had only 2 days so I chose to do a coastal village tour one day, and visit the penguin colony in Punihuil on the other day. Juan Pablo from Chiloe Etnico was my tour guide for both days. We journeyed from Castro, to Quinchao Island to Curaco de Velez, a small village, to Achao Town to visit an all-wooden church. We had lunch at a local restaurant, and came back to stop at another church and craft market in Quinchao. On that day I visited 3 churches that are UNESCO World Heritage sites. The next day Juan Pablo took me to a fish market in Ancud and then went to Punihuil, having lunch and taking a boat to see penguins. October is generally too early to see penguins since they are still nesting. But I was lucky to see 3 Magellan and 1 Humboldt, and also 3 Chilean dolphins, a sea otter, and many commarants. Juan Pablo spoke English well (not easy to find anyone who spoke English in Chiloe), and he was very nice and knowledgable about Chiloe. I had a great time. I highly recommend Chiloe Etnico to anyone who wants a good tour guide to visit Chiloe Island.

review_text: When searching and choosing tours and activities for my recent trip to Santiago de Chile, I was tempted to go for the unusual and wanted to experience what is not taken by the mass tourism. Perhaps what appeared as the most appealing in a new Spaniard travel website was the tour to the night life including the visit to bars and picturesque places. This activity happens only on Saturdays and is offered in Spanish languague . After pursuing this tour, I am proud to say that the main trait has been causing strong emotional reaction because of unexpectedness and plenty of positive surprises. I had an eye-opening experience under the guidance of tour guide LAURA CACERES from Tac Turismo, an easy-going and cheerful lady, who is sympathetic and very joyful providing her particular view as a local. We went to visit bars being the first in the Brasil district, where I was introduced to a young Chilean beverage that became typical in the last few years: the Terremoto (earthquake translated to English), which is prepared with white wine, granadine, pineapple icecream, fernet, and sometimes cognac and that came to existence after the tragic earthquake occurred in Chile during the 1985 year. Because of big size of the glass, the one served is called Cataclismo, and I have to say it really impacts as a drink. Secondly, the Bellavista district was even more jaw-dropping as the area sorrounding and inside the unique Patio Bellavista is not only bohemian but also emblematic as it constituts a landmark in Santiago. Having so many bars and restaurants as well as stores and crafts makes it an extremely lively and colorful area. Tour guide LAURA CACERES explained several local secrets and even vivid pieces of gossip making the walking startling! Finally, the Manuel Montt suburb located in Providencia turned out to be a stupendous place likewise. Cobblestoned streets and restaurants featuring traditional Chilean meals make the gold brooch of this activity for being introduced to the nightly life of Santiago. Review of: Tour Santiago by Night

review_text: We booked this tour one day In advance as we were at turistour’s office which is a meeting point for all the tours. I reserved the tour for the next day and confirmed time for the tour with the booking person. He said 9AM. I also checked the tour brochure which also said 9AM-3PM. Our ride showed up at 8AM. Our pick up person said tour is at 9 but pick up is at 8AM (This is not mentioned in the tour brochure). He refused to wait 15 minutes for us to get ready and suggested to do the afternoon tour. We had other plans in the afternoon. He suggested us to take taxi to the meeting point. Taxi cost us $15 which we had to pay ourselves. We got to the meeting point before 9AM and tour didn’t leave till 9.15. Our guide Jaime was very knowledgeable, clear to understand and funny. He provided information on Chile, different wine regions, Maipa Valley and history of Concha Y Toro winery. Once we got to the winery we were divided into separate English speaking and Spanish speaking tours. Our tour started right away and we joined 3 other people from other tour companies. Some people in our group had to wait another hour for their Spanish speaking tour. Tour is conducted by the staff at the winery. You get 3 wine tastings and grapes to taste with vineyard tour and a video demonstration. Staff is knowledgeable and kind. After the tour we waited 45 minutes-1 hour for the others to finish their tour. Then we met our guide near the restaurant and returned to the van. We got transferred back to the meeting point and then to the hotel. What has stuck out for us during this tour was the generosity of our guide Jaime. What had happened was that my daughter had left her sunglasses (Burberry) in the tour bus day before. I had called the tour company office in the evening and was told that bus is in the garage now, they will contact the driver and will know 7AM if the glasses are in the bus. Next morning I mentioned to the person that came to pick us up about glasses he said he will report it to the office. Once we got to the meeting point where company’s office is I asked our guide from the previous day if he knew anything about the glasses. He said office will contact me. We left for the tour and came back to the office after our 4 hours. I told Jaime that I need to check with the office if they have found my glasses. This was the first time Jaime had heard about the sunglasses story. He right away took matter into his hands and spoke with the office personnel in front of me. Office girl phoned the driver and found out that glasses are at the garage and I will have to take taxi and go pick them up. This garage was out of town somewhere. Jaime was generous enough to say that he is getting off work after dropping us off. He will go home and take his own car to pick up the glasses and drop them off at our hotel. Which he did. I usually don’t write reviews but this was something exceptional that someone has done for us. Turistour should be proud to have an employee like Jaime!! They need more employees like Jaime!! you are only getting 5* because of Jaime otherwise service was 3*!!
title: Shout out to our amazing guide Jaime for going extra mile in his own time !!

We got to the meeting point before 9AM and tour didn’t leave till 9.15. Our guide Jaime was very knowledgeable, clear to understand and funny. He provided information on Chile, different wine regions, Maipa Valley and history of Concha Y Toro winery. Once we got to the winery we were divided into separate English speaking and Spanish speaking tours. Our tour started right away and we joined 3 other people from other tour companies. Some people in our group had to wait another hour for their Spanish speaking tour. Tour is conducted by the staff at the winery. You get 3 wine tastings and grapes to taste with vineyard tour and a video demonstration. Staff is knowledgeable and kind. After the tour we waited 45 minutes-1 hour for the others to finish their tour. Then we met our guide near the restaurant and returned to the van. We got transferred back to the meeting point and then to the hotel. What has stuck out for us during this tour was the generosity of our guide Jaime. What had happened was that my daughter had left her sunglasses (Burberry) in the tour bus day before. I had called the tour company office in the evening and was told that bus is in the garage now, they will contact the driver and will know 7AM if the glasses are in the bus. Next morning I mentioned to the person that came to pick us up about glasses he said he will report it to the office. Once we got to the meeting point where company’s office is I asked our guide from the previous day if he knew anything about the glasses. He said office will contact me. We left for the tour and came back to the office after our 4 hours. I told Jaime that I need to check with the office if they have found my glasses. This was the first time Jaime had heard about the sunglasses story. He right away took matter into his hands and spoke with the office personnel in front of me. Office girl phoned the driver and found out that glasses are at the garage and I will have to take taxi and go pick them up. This garage was out of town somewhere. Jaime was generous enough to say that he is getting off work after dropping us off. He will go home and take his own car to pick up the glasses and drop them off at our hotel. Which he did. I usually don’t write reviews but this was something exceptional that someone has done for us. Turistour should be proud to have an employee like Jaime!! review_text: If I could give this more than 5 stars I would! This was the best thing we did in our 2+ weeks in Chile! Rod and Benito were great pilots and guides. The weather was expected to be bad for our original day so we changed the tour day and had a perfect weather day for 4 hour float plane flight from our hotel over the lakes region to Parque Pumalín, and Corcovado. We would not have been able to see what we saw in the those areas without flying. Rod & Benito picked us up, gave us the safety information and it was a very cautious and safe tour. We stopped for fuel and took off again for wonderful views through fjords seeing many waterfalls, dense trees and the magic national parks of Chile. We landed the float plane on a lake in the middle of the park and had a nice lunch with incredible views. I could post more pictures and videos because it was so beautiful! After lunch, we flew around and back to the lake in front of our hotel to land us back safely. Thanks Rod & Benito for a wonderful time! If you have the time and resources, this is a NOT TO MISS opportunity!

review_text: Wonderful team. They offer private or semi-private tours at affordable prices and with an experienced, professional and very attentive team. We did 4 tours with them. 1st tour was Portillo and Laguna del Inca with a wonderful barbecue at 3,000 meters of altitude… a unique experience. Throughout the way, our guide Diego explained fauna, flora, culture and regional stories. Arriving in Portillo, a paradisiacal view. Without a doubt, this is a tour that you cannot miss on your trip to Santiago. 2nd tour Valparaíso and Viña del Mar, our guide Juan, gave us an incredible experience. Going up and down the hills of Valparaíso, showing the most exclusive graffiti, and explaining a lot about the history of the place. In Viña del Mar we find a more modern look and also a lot of history. The experience of taking this tour with experienced guides is priceless. 3rd tour was Silêncio Andino, our guide Maurício, was of unique professionalism. On this tour we travel through the Cajón del Maipo region, making stops at waterfalls, villages and the whole way, besides being very beautiful, it has a lot of history and incredible landscapes. We closed the tour with a picnic in the middle of the Andes next to a beautiful waterfall... another incredible experience, which you cannot miss on your trip to Santiago The 4th tour was to visit the ski resort region. Farellones and Valle Nevado… even without snow the place is very beautiful. But the experience that our guide Juan gave us was truly incredible… explaining every detail of the path followed by a picnic at almost 3,000 meters of altitude to watch the sunset. Sunset in the Andes… wonderful, indescribable. This one cannot be missed on your trip. Going to Chile offers unique tours, cultural and adventure experiences.

review_text: Such great views and convenient to get up. The first time I went I was told the funicular was not working so I got a bus ticket and it let us up at top, last bus down at 7:30. Next day, the funicular was working, also to the top, last trip down 7:45. Beautiful view at the very top, but the best thing for me was exploring the hill. There are many trails all over with surprise views. I went right as fall was beginning and the colors of the vegetation was beautiful in the late afternoon sun. I believe someone mentioned here that it's a horrible place for dog lovers; it's true that there are a lot of dogs up there, many are skinny a few had sad wounds. As a major dog lover, I'm a major sucker for them, so I gave them some empanadas (about $2 each at stands on the hill) and they were very happy. But a lot of them are very very appreciative just to be petted. So I wouldn't necessarily avoid this place if you're a dog lover, just give them some food if you want or just pet them and show some affection. I had a wonderful time hiking all over with four dog friends.

review_text: I took a total of 4 tours with the agency, Farellones, Cavalgando nos Andes, Vinicola Alyan and Tour Valpo y Viña. I liked it from the first contact, I received very good service and they were very honest, they explained about all the tours, and which ones were possible to do for the dates I requested. The first tour was a panoramic tour of Farrellones and Valle Nevado, but we chose to stay only in Farellones, we went with the guide Rodrigo who explained different things to us about the landscape as we went up the mountain. While riding in the Andes, our guide was Diego, who made the trip to the riding location go by in the blink of an eye with all his knowledge about the history of Chile, as well as a great conversation. About the tour itself, it is something magical to be so close to the mountain that is imposing and the silence that brings peace, with stunning landscapes, it is difficult to put into words how magical this tour is. We went to Vinicola with the guide Maurício, and once again a lesson about the different communities we passed through until we reached Vinicola and a little more about the history of Santiago. And as we were early to start the tour in Alyan, he suggested making a quick stop, just to visit Vinicola Concha y Toro. And to finish, we visited Valparaíso and Viña del Mar, also with the guide Rodrigo. It was really worth it, because as the tours are done in 4x4 and with a maximum of 4 people, it is possible to have pleasant conversations and receive a lot of knowledge from the guides. review_text: Taken here on a tour as part of our visit to the area. The approach once off the main highway is down a dirt road across the salt flats. Just the length of this itself is amazing. At the reserve there is a car park, toilets and video of the area. There are then paths to walk so you can see the bird life. We took the main one straight out. Along this we saw small groups of flamingos, some 8 in total, plus a few gulls and some little small birds. The flamingos were gorgeous as were the small birds. Add to this we saw a rat and lizards, the later were very close and with pretty markings. Whilst the flamingo were lovely the little brown birds were nearly as special and the lizards had lovely markings. There are views away from the Andes towards a smaller range and the clouds of the salt flats, with the roads and hills behind was equally special.

review_text: Colque Tours was recommended by another agency in San Pedro which don’t provide the Uyuni tours + our hostel. We booked a 3 days and 2 night trip to Uyuni with Nelson at the Colque Tours office in San Pedro. After having visited different agencies and reading several reviews online we decided to go with them simply because they ensured various comfort that other agencies couldn’t provide. They have a lot of bad reviews online but all of these are more than 5 years old; the most recent ones are surprisingly good... With such cold temperature (-15 at night) and light clothes we were looking for a place to sleep with heating. We asked if we could rent sleeping bags, however Nelson promised that Colque Tours would have given us a double room with heating/hot water in Villa Mar (paying an additional fee of 5,000 Chilean pesos). review_text: I recently traveled through Chile using Fodor's guidebook. Cochamo Valley is the Yosemite of Chile, an amazing place, and surprisingly not in your book. All this lead us to hike into the valley and stay for a week at the wonderful Refugio Cochamo. The couple and their son built the lodge and have run it for eight years. Accommodation great, tasty organic whole wheat bread and homegrown veggies and very friendly. This valley is breathtaking: hikes, waterfalls, thousand meter walls and very old trees. Check it out. It's a don't miss destination. Anyway, I think this is super important destination and environmentally fragile. Thus I hope no road ever gets constructed in to it. Thanks to the Refugio Cochamó for all their efforts, trail building, rock climbing routes and unmistakeable passion for the area.

review_text: This museum visit was a perfect end to my day in Santiago. It's a hidden gem that not many tourists, locals, or even guides know about. And, it's FREE! Housed in a gorgeous location, this museum contains an absolutely stunning rotating collection of modern Latin American art and sculpture. All of the works were beautiful and thought-provoking. Upstairs is a permanent exhibition of more prominent artists like Dali and Chagall. The Dali sculptures- wow. The museum is also a perfect size to see everything in two hours or less and not get overwhelmed. The only issue I had here was that there is no information on the works. That would have been ideal, since all were incredibly interesting and I would have loved to delve deeper into the art. A few pieces have placards where you can scan a code with your phone and thus pull up information on an app, but all of it was in Spanish. Furthermore, all the placards that did have information were in Spanish and not translated. I could read the Spanish, but this might be a problem for some international visitors. I would encourage people to connect to the museum's wifi and Google pieces that you find interesting to get more information on them. review_text: This is the story of how we had our Honeymoon turned into a stress-filled few weeks by a company claiming to offer premium travel. BE WARNED. We found Cascada travel after doing some research and they seemed to get good reviews. After some correspondence with Fernanda, she provided various tour options we could do. During this process Fernanda was polite, helpful, answering our questions quickly. We decided on two trips - Ecocamp wildlife safari and the Stella Australis cruise. We chose the ecocamp 5 day safari which totalled more than US$4000 (superior dome). Unfortunately this did not turn out as we hoped and we felt was a waste of money, terrible service and we did not receive what was promised. We left for our honeymoon in Dec and while travelling between Chile and Argentina we received an email from Cascada on 29th Dec 2011 advising us that because of the dreadful forest fires inside Torres del Paine national park (that had started on 27th Dec) the ecocamp was still open but on alert, that they hoped things would improve so they didn’t have to evacuate the park but would update us as and when they knew more. We sent Fernanda and the Cascada 24hr emergency team an email asking what this meant for us. Specifically, if the park was closed what options would we be given and could we claim a refund for our unused trip. They responded by saying “... wait till Monday and see how the situation is doing and see if it well-worth to stick or not to the plan. The alternative is to cancel the trip and get in contact with your Travel Insurance and request for full refund due to this force majeure event at Torres del Paine NP.” Our first clue something wasnt right...usually a cancellation by the company is the responsibility of their insurance, not ours. On 30th Dec 2011 we received another email advising us that the park was being shut but they hoped it would be open by 3rd Jan so we could get in as per our booking. We asked what alternative options we had in case our trip was cancelled as we had also paid for a semi-private transfer with them to take us eventually to Punta Arenas to catch the cruise. They suggested other areas we could visit and that we had to make our own arrangements to get from El Calafate to Punta Arenas for our cruise. They again quoted the line that we should speak to our travel insurance company to claim the costs. We had numerous emails with them about this as this was not acceptable to leave us stranded when we had paid for the transfer services. Take note that we still hadn’t arrived or received any of the services of ecocamp (already paid over US$4000) and the US$240 semi-private transfer, which they were now saying they would not provide! On 3rd Jan 2012 we tried numerous times to call the various telephone numbers they had given us (none worked) so we could find out what was going on. Finally we got in touch and spoke to one of the Cascada staff who advised us that they would pick us up early the following morning from our hotel in El Calafate for the semi-private transfer to ecocamp. The driver arrived on time and we crossed the border without any problems. This is a service they outsource to another company. To be clear, we were told we would be ON OUR OWN if the park was closed with NO options for travel to our next destination (booked with Cascada!) and when they did decide to honour their obligations for transfer they NEVER TOLD US! If we hadn’t found a local travel agent who kindly sent Cascada a text message we would NOT have known about the transfer at all! When we arrived at the ecocamp office in Puerto Natales we met some of the staff who explained the current situation in the park. We plus approximately 30 other guests (who arrived soon after) were taken to a restaurant next door for lunch that they paid for. We then found out that the park would not open until 4th Jan 2012 so we would all be put in a hotel overnight. We stayed in the “If hotel” US$100 per room for one night including breakfast. Cascada provided dinner at a local restaurant which was less than mediocre and offered no options - Remember we are paying $1000/night for these excursions so a 3rd rate dinner is not acceptable! We finally got into the park on 4th Jan 2012 leaving us with 3nights (instead of 4) at the ecocamp. We lost over US$1,000 for the 1 night we didn’t stay in the ecocamp. After an uninspired 3 days in the ecocamp (please read my other review on this – do not spend money to stay at the ecocamp) we finally left. Cascada drove us to the cruise ship’s office in Punta Arenas. Since returning home we have spoken to our insurance company and, as we suspected, we are not covered for this sort of situation. They say that this type of claim is typically handled by the insurance of the vendor, not by private insurance so be warned when booking with Cascada as you may not be covered. The hotel we were put in, the lunch and dinner they provided were not to the standard you expect for the thousands of $$ we spent. And worst of all the terrible customer service we received from the various Cascada staff was unacceptable. They were difficult to deal with, were not willing to compromise or offer alternatives and have stated to many other guests that they will not refund any of of us. We learned by speaking to some insiders that it appears they do not have any insurance and are therefore deceiving innocent people who have saved for what was meant to be a great trip. Be warned: Cascada is great at getting your money but then customer service is far from what you would expect for the money. They treated us (and other guests) with no care. Please also read my review on the ecocamp before you book any trips using Cascada or stay at the ecocamp. Ecocamp is not worth the money. Save your money and stay somewhere with better value and staff that care. (You can book the Stella Australis cruise directly with the company and this was one of the highlights - highly recommended! - just don’t bother booking via Cascada). Review of: 5-Day Wildlife Safari Hola, Thanks for your feedback. Every feedback is important to us as we constantly seek to improve the quality of our service and to make our guests as happy as possible on their trip to South America. We are sorry to hear your trip was unpleasant due to the consequences of the terrible fire that took place in Summer 2011 and ravaged 176km2 (60 square miles) of the park. 400 people were evacuated in the park for which was the biggest fire in the history of the National Park. Unfortunately we had to evacuate EcoCamp and the information provided by the public authorities was unclear due to the “chaos” in the region. This led to the evacuation of the hotel despite the fact we were not directly affected by the fire. As the fire did not happen at EcoCamp, Cascada was not held responsible for refunding the guests. This rare force majeure event was handled as quickly as possible by our Customer Service (we had to help hundreds of guests traveling to Patagonia, including dozens of guests on-site). For every trip Cascada Expediciones provides clear information about the importance of travel insurance and we are pleased to offer a personalized experience for every guest to feel as safe as possible on their trip. We hope to welcome you again in Chile! Best regards, Timothy

We then found out that the park would not open until 4th Jan 2012 so we would all be put in a hotel overnight. We stayed in the “If hotel” US$100 per room for one night including breakfast. Cascada provided dinner at a local restaurant which was less than mediocre and offered no options - Remember we are paying $1000/night for these excursions so a 3rd rate dinner is not acceptable! We finally got into the park on 4th Jan 2012 leaving us with 3nights (instead of 4) at the ecocamp. We lost over US$1,000 for the 1 night we didn’t stay in the ecocamp. After an uninspired 3 days in the ecocamp (please read my other review on this – do not spend money to stay at the ecocamp) we finally left. Cascada drove us to the cruise ship’s office in Punta Arenas. Since returning home we have spoken to our insurance company and, as we suspected, we are not covered for this sort of situation. They say that this type of claim is typically handled by the insurance of the vendor, not by private insurance so be warned when booking with Cascada as you may not be covered. The hotel we were put in, the lunch and dinner they provided were not to the standard you expect for the thousands of $$ we spent. And worst of all the terrible customer service we received from the various Cascada staff was unacceptable. They were difficult to deal with, were not willing to compromise or offer alternatives and have stated to many other guests that they will not refund any of of us. We learned by speaking to some insiders that it appears they do not have any insurance and are therefore deceiving innocent people who have saved for what was meant to be a great trip. Be warned: Cascada is great at getting your money but then customer service is far from what you would expect for the money. They treated us (and other guests) with no care. Please also read my review on the ecocamp before you book any trips using Cascada or stay at the ecocamp. Ecocamp is not worth the money. review_text: Pueblito Los Dominicos is a wonderful place for visitors of all ages. It is a picturesque village where one can actually meet and commonly view the artist at their craft. As others mentioned, do not expect flea market or street vendor prices, but rather high quality, long-lasting goods at reasonable prices. Off the top of my head I recall viewing seemingly unlimited varieties of ceramic goods, recycled art, fine and fashion jewelry, handbags, fabric art, copper goods, canvas and wood painting, furniture, and leather products. I read that there are nearly 160 different vendors, and I believe it! There is an unusually large cage (larger than the size of my hotel room) filled with all sorts of birds (chickens, pigeons, doves, peacocks, quail) in the entrance that will entertain the youngest of guests. There is a man with a large hand-cranked, wooden music box and parrot who walks around entertaining the children with crepe paper toy parachutes and other goodies. It's fun to watch this pied piper interact with the children. Benches are placed throughout the village for those who wish to rest their feet and enjoy the sights and sounds around them. One could walk swiftly through the village in a half-hour (and then kick oneself) or spend several hours speaking with the friendly artisans and admiring their wares. We purchased wine and several different empandas at the open-air restaurant and found them to be fair priced and adequate. I would not plan eating a meal there, but it's quite sufficient for a snack and beverage. Los Dominocos is the last stop on the Red line of the metro and is situated near a lovely park and playground. I purchased a beautiful arpilleras from the Fundacion Solidarid, one of the first stalls near the entrance. According to the documentation that accompanied it: "The first arpilleras appeared very soon after the military coup of 1973, when Chile lost its long-standing democracy and were sewn by the mothers, wives and sisters of "disappeared" people during the dictatorship...Many arpilleristas have formed workshops, where the mone received from the sale of the arpilleras is distributed equally among all the participants of the group." I will proudly display it in my home, cherishing it, and the memories of my visit to Chile.

review_text: Yes, we've been to Yellowstone, but this is different (in a good way). It definitely is worth the 1 1/2 hr bumpy trip on packed dirt road in the dark, and we easily drove it ourselves in a rental pickup. You don't need a 4x4, or even that high of clearance. We left our hotel at 0500, in the long line of tourist vans heading out the same way. We peeled off down the road to the thermal baths to get away from the car lights so I could get some night sky photography. We ended up arriving near the tail end of all the vans and buses, which was actually nice for buying our tickets and using the bathroom. Sunrise was scheduled for 0715 and we arrived about 0700. You definitely need to get there before the sun comes over the mountains, so you can see all the steam, but also then, to appreciate the difference that the sunlight makes for the atmosphere and photos. But as we did, you don't have to get there when it's still dark. Even in "summer", it's very cold before sunrise, and layers and gloves were very welcome. We passed on swimming in the thermal baths there. We spent about an hour overall, wandering and taking photos. The drive back in the early morning was great, to see what you missed in the dark, and to stop and take pictures along the waterways - flamingos, ducks, geese and viscachas!

I am an experienced backpacker and this was one of the most dangerous trails I had been on in a long time. Mostly due to the steep inclines that are pure mud made worse by incessant rain. Along the way I got to see Alerces that were 3000 years old. It is a very green and beautiful place if you don't mind getting soaked. I did make it to the lake.

review_text: We had requested a shore excursion from San Antonio along the coast to Santiago Airport several months before our cruise. However, we were told several times prior to the cruise that this would not be possible due to unrest in Chile. Therefore, we just booked a transfer for $70 pp and paid a $40 deposit, leaving a $100 balance that the company requested be paid onsite in cash. However, a few days before we arrived in San Antonio, we were told that the situation had improved and were offered the tour, which we accepted at $110 pp, leaving a balance of $180. Unfortunately, our ship was unable to dock in San Antonio and went instead to Valparaiso, arriving much later. As soon as the Captain told us of this change, we contacted South Excursions and let them know that we would not be able to do the tour, but would go straight to the airport. We were told that, although the van was on its way to San Antonio, it would be turned around and this would be "no problem." We were surprised to be met at Valparaiso by both a guide and driver and once again reiterated that we were going straight to the airport where we had a day room at the Holiday Inn attached to the airport. As we approached the airport, the guide asked for our balance, and we were shocked to hear that we were being charged the entire cost of the tour we did not take! We asked to speak to the representative with whom we had booked the transfer. She told us that she had been expecting the call and had checked with her "bosses," and this would be the charge. She agreed that most all companies make an exception to their refund policies when a ship is unable to dock at the scheduled port, but that this company does not. We expressed our displeasure to no avail. We probably should have refused to pay the increased balance, but since the representative said that she would try again to have it reduced to the transfer price and send us a refund, we paid. Upon arrival, the driver was unable to find a parking spot and circled the airport three times in heavy traffic. We noticed that other vans, buses, and taxis were taking a different entrance marked for authorized vehicles and asked if our van was authorized. The answer was no. To his credit, he eventually parked in a parking garage and walked us with our luggage to the entrance. Once home, we received an email saying that there would be no refund. This appears to be a Miami-based company that contracts with tour providers throughout South America and leaves these representatives with no leeway regardless of the situation. It was obvious that our representative was embarrassed, but had no authority to change the situation. The Miami-based "bosses" seem to have no understanding of customer service, claiming that they still had to pay the guide and driver whether we took the tour or not. True, but why send a guide when they knew that there would be no need? And why were we not told that we would be charged for the tour when we contacted the representative earlier that day instead of being told that it was "no problem?" Had we known this, we would have simply canceled the entire thing, found alternative transportation and challenged any charges they tried to impose. Our advice is steer clear of South Excursions! Dear Brenda and Tom, Sorry that you feel that way, but it was not our fault that the cruise company changed the arrival port from San Antonio to Valparaiso, we actually sent our vehicle and guide from one city to another in order to be able to provide you with the service that you booked from us, cities that are over an hour a way from each other, we did all what we could to provide you with a pleasant time. As our vehicle and guide were already in service, we were not able to just cancel the day for them and drop our guide as you suggest, it's not really fair for the tour guide, so the cost of the service was still the same. I hope you understand our point of view, we have a reasonable refund and cancellation policy that you were aware about when the service was booked, if the tour or service it's changed or cancel with such a short notice, we are not able to provide you with the partial refund that you request, as our cost are still the same. PS: We are not a Miami based company, we are located in Valparaiso/Viña del Mar Chile Best regards, Javier SouthExcurisons

review_text: We use the agency's services in Colombia. We had no problems in Cartagena, the tours were amazing. In San Andres, we took a shared boat ride, which was actually a fishing boat that they placed around 20 people. The next day, we did dive and had parasail scheduled, we became aware of an accident that occurred with the parasail in the same week, but at no time the agency was transparent with us, on the contrary, learned from another tourist that the tours were not happening and only when I asked the attendant who informed me that it would not, I would go to the port atoa, because they sent me the voucher and I believed that everything was fine. The next day we had a walk from the dawn, we stayed 1h waiting to pick us up and ngm appeared, after we were informed that it was canceled. I understand that the time is very early, before the expedition, but just as at the dive the company of San Andres got in contact with us, I think the minimum would be someone to have our contact and warn us. Sentimos muito pelos transtornos vividos durante sua experiência em San Andrés. Agradecemos por compartilhar seu relato — ele nos ajuda a identificar falhas importantes. Sabemos o quanto isso impacta uma viagem tão planejada, e já estamos revendo nossos processos. Ficamos felizes que tenha aproveitado os passeios em Cartagena, e esperamos ter a chance de reconquistar sua confiança no futuro. Esperamos voce nos nossos outros destinos.

review_text: We travelled with Navimag on their four night/five day voyage from Puerto Montt on the Puerto Eden. The glacier is definitely worth seeing and the approach on small boats amongst the ice flows was unforgettable. We were lucky with the weather both at the glacier and en route and so were able to make the most of the impressive scenery, including the erupting volcano near Chaiten, and wildlife - seals, altbatrosses and other birds. On the return journey, Navimag provided a coach tour to Puerto Aisen, a local waterfall and a 'barbeque' lunch, all of which were good. The atmosphere on board was good and passengers were able to visit the bridge as well as take part in various activities. The captain was good and very hands on. However, the boat was quite old and not kept very clean. The two of us shared a four bunk cabin with its own shower room. It was all pretty basic and the food on board was adequate at best. We sat on deck for long periods but when the weather was bad, there was nowhere else quiet and comfortable to go. The staff were OK but no effort was made to communicate in anything other than Spanish so we relied on fellow passengers. You get what you pay for - I guess it was just about OK for the price.

review_text: We met Cristian in the street at one of the stalls, and he suggested we might like to do a walking tour with him. We did this on the next day for 5 hours (including a short stop for a sandwich). We wandered around the historic part of town meeting many of the artists, then went on a local bus to the street markets. It was great and we would recommend everyone do one of these walking tours, even if you only have a couple of hours to spare. It is the best way to see Valparaiso, and Cristian is a very good guide with excellent English. The only issue was that he didn't have a set charge, and just said to pay him what we thought it was worth. We didn't have a clue as to what was appropriate. We just hope that what we paid was okay. It was a pleasure to share with you that morning. We thank you for trusting us and for the unforgettable moments we live together in Valparaíso. One of the advantages of doing private tours is to have the chance to adapt the route and times to your interests and rhythm. Please say hi to your husband!

review_text: I found Mauricio - Chilean Wine Lovers - through TripAdvisor. A big THANKS to all who recommended him!!! We were a group of 10 wine lovers and we had an outstanding time!! I had originally scheduled Mauricio for 3 days, but we liked his arrangements, attitude, and tours so much, we added 3 more days! Mauricio is extremely knowledgeable about the history, geography, wines, economy, and everything else about his country. He shared a great deal with us and it was extremely interesting. He was funny, accommodating, and I highly recommend using him if you need a guide ANYWHERE!! The Colchagua tour to Clos Apalta, Montes and Viu Manent was awesome! The wines and food were outstanding and the views were breathtaking. The Andes are quite a magnificent backdrop for the beautiful wineries we toured. Besides the Colchagua tour, we also tried Chilean Wine Tours High Maipo tour, which was GREAT. The lunch at Mojaito was delicious, country food with some great wines provided by Mauricio. Mauricio also arranged custom trips at our request. There was a great trip to a very cool market town, Pamaire, and an amazing lunch at Las Naranjas - thank you for the Carmenere, Mauricio. Then our Valpairaiso tour! Very, very interesting port city with really neat art/bohemian areas to walk around. A terrific meal at Odo Pacifico overlooking the harbor.
