review_text: Nuestra visita (mi marido, mi hija y yo) fue el 10 de julio, día de neblina y mucho frío. Aún cuando muchos animales por el frío se refugiaron en sus espacios quedando fuera de la vista de los visitantes, el lugar es tan amplio y con tantos espacios, que encanta de todos modos a quienes nos gusta aprender de los animales en un entorno que no es tan pequeño como otros zoológicos. Otro comodín del zoológico es el espacio de animatronix de dinosaurios, que en gran parte tienen movimiento y hasta sonido, éste recorrido incluido en el valor de la entrada finaliza con réplicas de fósiles, se nota la preocupación del personal por todos los espacios del zoológico. Dentro del recinto hay lugares donde se vende comida y/o snack, más de un espacio de baños, incluso baños tamaño pequeño para los niños, y una tienda de souvenirs para quienes necesitan un consuelo a la hora de irse. La superficie del lugar es extensa, pero a la entrada entregan un mapa para ir recorriendo de acuerdo a lo sugerido, o a intereses propios, y existe una aplicación para hacer el recorrido junto con un apoyo virtual. Otro comodín que tiene este zoológico para los pequeños es el espacio de granja, donde se puede ingresar sin barreras a estar en contacto con varios animales. Our visit (My husband, my daughter and I) was on July 10, the day was with haze and very cold. Even though many animals from the cold took refuge in their spaces, being out of sight of the visitors, the place is so wide and has so many different areas, that it enchants anyway. Another plus, the animals have not so small places as other zoos. Another plus of the zoo is the dinosaur animation space, which is large and the dinosaurs have movement and even sound, this attraction is included in the value of the entrance, and it ends with replicas of fossils. You can tell that the staff worries about all places of the zoo. Within the enclosure there are places where food and / or snacks are sold, more than one bathroom space, small bathrooms, and a souvenir shop for those who need a comfort at the time of leaving. The surface of the place is extensive, but at the entrance you'll have a map to go according to the suggested route, or to your own interests, and an app exists to make the route along with a virtual support. Another place that this zoo has for the little ones is the space of the farm, where you can get in touch without barriers.

review_text: I travelled aboard the Ocean Nova with Antarctica XXI in early December 2015. The trip is definitely not a trip for the luxury traveler and for those in poor physical shape. I travelled with an older parent and we found the trip to be well planned and very enjoyable. You arrive in Punta Arenas, Chile and meet up with your group for a briefing and to try on boots for the trip. You are given a free bag and luggage scale which come in handy since you are only allowed 20kg for all your luggage. That night at dinner you are told if the flight is taking off in the morning or not, ours did. They have tour plans set up if the flight is delayed. The flight over is only 2 hours. Once you get off the airplane you walk about 1 mile down to the zodiacs where you get a life vest that you use all week and you are transported to the boat. They did have a special vehicle for those unable to walk. The initial strait crossing is fairly rough, so pack any necessary seasickness meds - the ship doctor also has them. Each day there are screens all over the ship that tell you what is going on and where you are going that day. There is also a board outside the dining hall that tells you the activities for the day. They offer kayaking and snowshoeing that you can sign up for in advance or on the ship if spots are still available. The ship often changes what is happening each day based on weather. They can mail postcards for you and they rent hiking poles in the shop onboard - I used these 2 of the 6 days as some of the hikes were quite intense uphill and the snow was melting making it somewhat icy. It was cold around 0 C or 32-29F but the wind is bad and so bringing many layers is useful. Bring a backup camera, it is common for cameras to act up in the cold weather as mine did. We saw amazing wildlife - seals, orcas, humpbacks, 3 species of penguins and many types of birds (as well as a few other types of whale). They also sell some basic gear on board (gloves, hats, fleeces, etc - but it's pricey). We didn't get to Port Lockroy because of ice but we did get a chance to visit the Russian station by the airstrip where they sell some magnets and postcards and you can stamp your postcard. (They have stamps on the ship too.) Bring ginger cookies or candies with you - they ship didn't have any and some of the nights when the water was choppy it would have been helpful. The food was excellent. The bar was great and the panorama room was a fun place to hang out with your fellow passengers and watch the animals as the ship cruises along. Don't expect wifi as service is spotty. Guides were great and gave some very interesting presentations each night. Overall, this isn't a luxury trip but a true expedition where things can change at a moments notice. As long as you are prepared for going with flow and enjoying the view, then you will have a great time.

There were comfortable sofas from which we could admire the entire starry sky. And what a sight that was alone! It's incredible! Claudio explained us in detail and very competently different planets and stars. We were also allowed to admire these in more detail with 2 large telescopes. After the conclusion of the star show, which lasted about 2 hours, there was a photo session with a total of 4 souvenir photos. And last but not least, we were served an aperitif with rich appetizers by a warm fire. We are thrilled what an unforgettable evening we had the pleasure of experiencing thanks to Claudio and Maurizio's sympathetic and dedicated efforts. We highly recommend this tour! Thank you again!

review_text: This walking tour gave me a nice introduction to Santiago's rich history and beautiful city center. We started at the presidential palace and worked our way through the walk streets, central park, old Spanish church and beautiful public library. Eugene was very relaxed, but keen to share his enthusiasm for the city. He got to know everyone in the small group without being cheesy. I highly recommend this tour if you are new to the city, want to engage a bit with its history and get some very helpful recommendations for other sites.
